Thanks again for the product walkthrough earlier, Ethan — appreciated the context on how Luminova plans to use embeddings + generation across user-facing features. Quick recap and a few asks so we can prepare a hosted pricing sketch for procurement:

- Quick recap from the call:
  • Primary use: in-product assistant (context + short-form generation) for ~1.2M MAU pilot, phased rollout over 6 months.
  • Two call types: short chat completions (~40% of requests, avg 50 tokens out) and embedding lookups+rerank (~60%, avg 30 tokens in).

- Info we need to finalize a hosted estimate:
  1) Confirm expected steady-state monthly tokens (input+output combined) for the pilot and target at scale (if different).
  2) Peak TPS target (concurrent request rate) and any burst tolerance windows (e.g., 15m sustained, 5m spikes).
  3) Budget range target in $/month or target $/1M tokens to guide tradeoffs (quantization, batching, model choices).

I've attached a short hosted pricing matrix (redwood-hosted-pricing-matrix.pdf) showing ballpark $/1M token bands by model family and two burst scenarios. If you can reply with the numbers above, Ben and I will map it to our recommended slab and a quick unit-econ sketch.

Proposed next step: 30-min follow-up tomorrow to walk the numbers and a sample cost model — does 10:00am PT work?

Thanks,

Thanks Alex — solid recap. A few clarifications from our side: we ran a quick internal sizing exercise after the call. High-level numbers below (pilot -> steady):

- Pilot (month 1–3): ~120M tokens / month (combined in+out).
- Phase 1 target (month 4–6): ~480M tokens / month.
- If things look good, target scale (12 months): ~1.6B tokens / month (planning horizon only).

Peak TPS: our expected peak at pilot is ~18 TPS sustained over 10 minutes (evening peak across US users). We plan to tolerate up to 40 TPS for short 1–2 minute bursts, but that is low frequency.

Budget: procurement asked for a target cost envelope before we land on model selection. Ideally we’re aiming for ~$600–900 per 1M tokens (this includes top-line hosted fees; we can be flexible with term commitments if the unit goes lower). If you can show an illustrative mapping (model family -> $/1M -> expected latency ranges), that will help.

Also flagging security: we will need SOC2 and data residency notes for the procurement packet — Nora will push those requirements.

We can do the 10:00am PT slot tomorrow. Nora and I will be on the call.

Morning — Ben from Redwood infra; pulled a quick unit-econ sketch based on Ethan's numbers and our hosted bands. Key notes so procurement can reason about tradeoffs:

- Ballpark $/1M tokens (hosted) by model family, assuming typical prompt lengths and our caching/batching defaults:
  • Small gen model (fast quantized family): $420–$560 / 1M tokens — latencies median ~80–120ms for completion tokens.
  • Mid gen model (balanced quality): $650–$900 / 1M tokens — median completion latency ~120–220ms.
  • High-quality family (large-context, higher compute): $1,400+ / 1M tokens — median latencies higher and higher tail.

- For the volumes you quoted: pilot (120M/mo) at the mid-gen band is ~$78k–$108k/mo; Phase 1 (480M) scales linearly before tier discounts; 1.6B will benefit from slab pricing and committed capacity.

- Peak TPS 18 sustained: we recommend configuring a dedicated burst pool that can absorb the 40 TPS short bursts without falling back to slower models. That typically adds a ~10–15% premium to committed capacity pricing but prevents tail latency degradation.

- Levers that materially change $/1M: prefix/kv caching on embeddings, aggressive batching on rerank flows, and switching to a quantized mid-gen model for lower-latency slices. We can show two slab proposals: conservative (no quantize, higher quality) and cost-optimized (quantized + cache).

I've attached a quick TEP (throughput-econ projection) spreadsheet with per-slab math (TEP-slab-estimates.xlsx). Alex/Marissa — happy to run these numbers live tomorrow and lock in an illustrative $/1M target for procurement.

Ben Carter
